social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 20 pack-years, quit 8 years ago

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented. Frustrated and scared.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Bilateral mild facial weakness — forehead sparing absent (lower face predominantly but forehead mildly involved). No ptosis. Gag reflex diminished. Dysarthria mild.
neurological_exam.motor: Moderate bilateral lower extremity weakness: hip flexion 3+/5, knee extension 4/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5. Upper extremities: 4/5 throughout.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal paresthesias. Reduced pinprick and vibration in stocking distribution to mid-calf bilaterally.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Global areflexia — absent bilaterally at all tendon reflexes.
neurological_exam.additional: FVC: 2.4 L (predicted 3.6 L — 67%). NIF: -35 cmH2O. Currently stable but 10-day course with prior diabetic neuropathy complicates picture.

patient.chief_complaint: Ten-day rapidly progressive leg weakness and paresthesias with areflexia in a diabetic man, preceded by respiratory illness.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. G. is a 58-year-old man with known mild diabetic peripheral neuropathy presenting with a 10-day history of rapidly worsening leg weakness. Two weeks before presentation, he had a 5-day upper respiratory illness. On the third day of recovery, he noticed new bilateral foot numbness more severe than his usual diabetic neuropathy. Over the following week, weakness rapidly progressed — he went from difficulty with stairs to being unable to walk without bilateral support. He noticed bilateral facial drooping when shaving. He has difficulty swallowing solids over the past 3 days. He denies respiratory distress at rest. His wife noted that his new symptoms are distinctly different from his usual diabetic foot tingling — she says he could previously walk normally. His neurologist saw him 3 months ago for diabetic neuropathy and noted only trace foot vibration loss; no weakness at that time. The rapid tempo and ascending nature of current symptoms strongly suggest an acute superimposed process.

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Glucose 142 mg/dL (H), HbA1c 7.2% % (H), CRP 16.1 mg/L (H), ESR 38 mm/hr (H), Mycoplasma pneumoniae IgM Positive  (H).

findings.finding: DML 6.1 ms (prolonged); CV 40 m/s (reduced); CMAP 3.8 mV (borderline reduced)
SNAP reduced amplitude — baseline sural absent is expected in diabetic neuropathy, but median sensory SNAP loss suggests new acute process
Absent in bilateral peroneal; prolonged (>60 ms) in bilateral median

quantitative_data.pattern: Acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy superimposed on pre-existing diabetic neuropathy

specialized_test.impression: Acute inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (AIDP/GBS) superimposed on pre-existing diabetic peripheral neuropathy. The acute proximal demyelinating features (absent F-waves, absent H-reflex, prolonged DMLs) are clearly beyond what is expected from diabetic neuropathy alone. This is moderate GBS with background diabetic neuropathy complicating interpretation.
recommended_actions: Background neuropathy does not affect GBS treatment — initiate IVIG

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 142 mmH2O. WBC: 4 cells/mm3 (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 55 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose: 62 mg/dL (ratio 0.67). Gram stain: No organisms.

findings.finding: CMAP amplitude stable at 2.0 mV — no further axonal loss

output.impression: NCS stable — no ongoing axonal injury. Patient appears to be plateauing. Consistent with IVIG response.

output.rhythm_summary: Predominantly sinus tachycardia. Intermittent sinus bradycardia episodes at night.
output.impression: Significant but manageable autonomic instability. No life-threatening arrhythmia. Continue telemetry.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP superimposed on pre-existing diabetic peripheral neuropathy (post-Mycoplasma)

differential.key_features: Acute onset over 10 days; bilateral facial weakness; global areflexia new; HbA1c only 7.2% — insufficient explanation
No sensory level, no UMN signs, areflexia
Acute 10-day onset — too rapid for CIDP

optimal_actions.expected_finding: Acute demyelinating AIDP superimposed on background diabetic neuropathy
Mycoplasma IgM positive; HbA1c mildly elevated — T2DM not the acute cause
Above threshold but declining — close monitoring needed
Mildly elevated protein with normal cells — albumino-cytologic dissociation

critical_actions: Do not attribute rapid progression to diabetic neuropathy — tempo and pattern (facial diplegia, global areflexia) clearly indicate acute GBS
Initiate IVIG without delay — pre-existing neuropathy does not affect treatment decision
ICU admission for respiratory monitoring — monitor serially
contraindicated_actions: Delaying IVIG waiting for resolution of 'diabetic flare'
key_reasoning_points: The KEY moderate-difficulty challenge: distinguishing acute GBS from worsening diabetic neuropathy — facial diplegia, global areflexia, and rapid 10-day progression are NOT diabetic neuropathy features
Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a well-recognized GBS trigger, especially following upper respiratory illness
Background diabetic neuropathy complicates NCS interpretation but does not change management — AIDP features are still identifiable
Anti-GD1b antibodies associated with Mycoplasma-triggered GBS
